Jasmine —

Quick note as we look at our renewal (renewal window in Jan): demand is spiking earlier than expected. We estimate a 2–3x usage uplift during our Q1 launch in Feb. Before we draft an amendment, two asks from procurement/finance: 1) a short-term price hold for the first 90 days post-renewal to avoid sticker-shock while we onboard; 2) surge protection (rate cap and guaranteed burst pool) so we have predictable costs for the promotional period.

We're open to committing more if we can get a temporary price hold and some credits for the ramp. Procurement copied for formal details.

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the forecast. High-level reaction: we can design a short, conditional program that balances your need for predictability with our unit economics. Proposed structure (summary):

- Surge Shield (90-day): temporary price hold at current rates for first 90 days after renewal, triggered by your Feb launch window.
- Concession Ladder: incremental credits tied to committed uplift (e.g., 25% credit if commit increases by 30%, 40% credit at 60% uplift). Credits apply to overage and can be used against invoices in the following quarter.
- Commit Flexline: a 12-month commit with a built-in true-up cadence (30/60/90 day checks) to allow smoothing; early-exit on volume miss with prorated clawback capped at X% of the annual value.
- Burst Pool: reserved burst capacity (N GPUs equivalent) for 120 days with measured throttle/burst pricing and a soft cap to prevent runaway spend.

I attached a one-page concession ladder and a draft amendment. Ben and Marissa are looped in to coordinate pricing math and internal approvals. If this looks close, we can convert to a formal amendment and run through legal/procurement.

Next steps: can you confirm the uplift band you expect (conservative and optimistic) and procurement's tolerance for a 12-month commit with true-up?

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu

Adding the numbers side — Alex, rough math attached is calibrated to the forecast you shared. Two important constraints from our side: the price hold only makes sense if the commit uplift is real (we can tier it) and the concession credit is structured as a one-off invoice credit vs. ongoing discounted unit price. That keeps the baseline pricing consistent for both parties.

We suggest three tiers:
- Tier A (30% commit uplift): 10% credit applied to overage (quarterly invoice) + access to Burst Pool at discounted burst rate for 60 days.
- Tier B (60% uplift): 20% credit + 120-day Burst Pool + price hold for 90 days.
- Tier C (90%+ uplift): 30% credit, 180-day Burst Pool, and a temporary rate cap for peak tokens.

I'll flag commercial approval for Tier B as our target — it aligns with what Jasmine proposed and keeps the risk mutual.

Ben

1) We prefer credits to be applied as a true rebate (on final invoice) rather than a persistent price change.
2) The price hold window needs to be clearly tied to usage milestones (not calendar dates) so we can't be on the hook for long tail usage.
3) Can you confirm the clawback cap percent and the true-up schedule in writing (we need wording for our finance team)?

If you can send a marked amendment with the concession ladder incorporated, we'll run it through our internal review.

Elena / Alex — appreciated. I've uploaded a marked amendment that reflects the procurement asks and commercial tiers (attached). Key clarifications in the doc:

- Credits: structured as one-time invoice rebates tied to uplift tier and paid within 45 days of quarter close.
- Price-hold trigger: usage milestone (>= 40% increase month-over-month for launch month) or official launch date, whichever occurs first — we can include a safe-harbor clause for reporting delays.
- Clawback cap: prorated clawback capped at 12% of the annual contract value in the case of sustained under-delivery.
- True-up cadence: 30/90/180 day checkpoints with a formal invoicing true-up at 90 days.

I've also proposed a hybrid Tier B as our recommended path: 20% one-time credit, 120-day Burst Pool, and a 90-day price hold. If CypherData signs off, we'll push the amendment as a DocuSign envelope and book the deal in HubSpot (DEAL-4821).
